Your Mission
Join Stryker’s R&D Simulation team and help shape the future of orthopaedic medical technology. During this Medical Engineering final thesis, you will apply numerical simulation methods to support the development of innovative implants and contribute to projects that have a direct impact on patient care. You will gain hands-on experience with modern engineering technologies, work alongside experienced experts, and develop valuable skills in simulation, biomechanical analysis, and product development. This is an excellent opportunity for students interested in Biomedical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Medical Engineering, or Biomechanics to build practical experience in a global MedTech environment.
What You'll Do
Support numerical simulations using Finite Element Analysis (FEA), musculoskeletal modelling, and CAD tools
Define physiological loading conditions and failure scenarios through scientific literature reviews and research activities
Evaluate implant design concepts and support validation activities for medical devices
Collaborate with engineers to align simulation and testing activities throughout product development
Contribute to technical documentation, reporting, and presentation of project results
What You'll Bring
Currently pursuing a Master's degree in Biomedical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Medical Engineering, Biomechanics, Materials Engineering, or a related field
Basic knowledge of Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and/or musculoskeletal modelling
Initial experience with Ansys, Abaqus, AnyBody, or comparable simulation software
Familiarity with CAD tools such as Creo or SolidWorks
Good English language skills (minimum B2), German language skills (B2) are beneficial
What's In It for You
Paid six-month full-time master thesis
Start date: March 2027
Location: Schönkirchen (near Kiel)
Flexible working hours and attractive holiday allowance
Mentoring and training to support your growth
Hands-on projects with real-world impact in an international environment
Please note: The project deals with current and sensitive development topics, so a confidentiality agreement (Sperrvermerk) will be required for your master thesis.
Application Process
Please upload all application documents (current CV/resume, and transcript of records are required) either as one combined file or as separate files in the “Resume/CV” section of the application form. Unfortunately, additional documents cannot be uploaded after submission.
We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals, regardless of ethnic, national, or social background, gender, disability, age, or sexual identity.
Germany Pay Range:
Schonkirchen/Kiel 35Std : €2.222,85 EUR Monthly
If you’d like to learn more about the compensation associated with this opportunity, your recruiter will be happy to walk you through the details as you progress through the hiring process.

e03f28e7899b.text:
Stryker are delighted to be hiring talented Software Engineers for our “R&D Graduate Programme” – to begin in September 2027.
Applications close: Friday 24th October 2026.
Please ensure your CV includes your academic results or current trending results (if final results are not yet available).
The “R&D Graduate Programme” is a 24-month structured graduate development programme in the R&D function. The programme rotates on a 6-month rotating assignment basis in order to learn and develop the basic knowledge and skills in the various engineering areas of expertise. The position rotates on a 6 monthly assignment basis:
Design
Advanced Operations / Research and Technology Development
Advanced Quality Engineering
Engineering Services (CAD/Prototype/Test Lab)
What Are We Looking For?
Dedicated achievers : People who thrive in a fast-paced environment and will stop at nothing to ensure a project is complete and meets regulations and expectations.
Curious learners . People who seek out cutting-edge research and information to expand and enhance their ability to develop new ideas into reality.
Collaborative partners . People who build and leverage cross-functional relationships to bring together ideas, information, use cases, and industry analyses to develop best practices.
During each rotational assignment participants will be responsible for:
Software:
Translating user needs to design inputs/specifications and producing component and sub-system level designs.
Owning the design, implementation, and testing of software modules, and performing associated software development tasks (configuration management, issue/bug tracking, and risk management).
Using version control to keep an easily traceable and documented history of development.
Using standard software methodologies to ensure code is readable, understandable and maintainable.
Investigation, design, development and implementation of new manufacturing processes and technology.
Handover of new processes from development to production.
Debugging and correcting design issues using independent judgment.
Independently balancing design trade-offs while designing a component of the system.
What You Need?
Candidates must have already attained or be on course to attain a 2.1 result in a Level 8 or above Software/ Computer Engineering Engineering course or related discipline.
Candidates must have/will have attained the above between June 2025 and Sept 2027 .
Self-starter with demonstrated efficient work methods, analytical & problem-solving skills, and ability to handle multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
The individual should enjoy working in a fast paced, dynamic and results orientated team environment.
Strong communication skills with the ability to effectively work cross-functionally and with global teams.
Benefits of Working in Stryker:
Secure a place on our Graduate Programme and you’ll enjoy a remuneration package that is unsurpassed, including:
Permanent Contract .
Annual Target Bonus .
Share Option Scheme .
Pension Scheme .
Health Care .
E xcellent opportunity for Progression and Development.
Hybrid Working.
Employee Assistance Programme.
Employee Resource Groups, and Sports and Social Groups.
Training and support with a dedicated mentor from day one .
Stryker
Stryker is one of the world’s leading medical technology companies and is dedicated to helping healthcare professionals perform their jobs more efficiently while enhancing patient care. Stryker is committed to delivering exceptional results to patients so they can continue to live healthy, active lifestyles.
A wide and diverse range of Stryker products are manufactured in Ireland including hip and knee system implants, bone cement, surgical blades and micro-rotary burs which are used for cutting, drilling, burring, and shaping bone and soft tissue during orthopaedic, spine, ear, nose and throat plastic surgery. Our neurovascular Ireland product pipeline represents a broad offering of detachable coils for the treatment of haemorrhagic stroke (the rupture of a blood vessel in the brain) and ischemic stroke (a blockage in a blood vessel in the brain).
Stryker offers results-driven people a place where they can make a difference. It is our privilege to create medical technology that exceeds our customers’ expectations and improves peoples’ lives around the world.
We give employees the opportunity to develop their career based on each individual’s strengths, performance and potential, including the possibility to move geographically, functionally, laterally, and vertically. Stryker is a career destination for engaged passionate and talented people who seek innovation, growth, and opportunity.
# IJ
Ireland: €44,000 EUR Annual
At Stryker, we believe transparency helps candidates make confident decisions about their next career step. Compensation is an important part of that process and we want to be clear about how pay is determined. The compensation information posted for this role may be presented as a salary range or a fixed amount depending on the role. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for incentive compensation (such as bonus and/or commissions where applicable), along with Stryker’s comprehensive benefits package.
If you’d like to learn more about the salary or the benefits associated with this role, your recruiter will be happy to walk you through the details as you progress through the hiring process.

Deine Mission
Du möchtest mit deinem Studium echten Einfluss auf die Medizintechnik nehmen? In dieser sechsmonatige Abschlussarbeit unterstützt du unser biomechanisches Testlabor bei der Entwicklung und Prüfung medizinischer Produkte. Dabei sammelst du wertvolle Praxiserfahrung in einem internationalen Umfeld, arbeitest an innovativen Projekten und lernst, wie Produktsicherheit, Forschung und Entwicklung zusammenwirken. Gleichzeitig erhältst du Einblicke in moderne Testmethoden, zukunftsweisende Technologien und die Entwicklung von Medizinprodukten, die das Leben von Patientinnen und Patienten weltweit verbessern.
Deine Aufgaben
Du unterstützt die Planung und Durchführung biomechanischer Produktsicherheitstests für medizinische Produkte.
Du wirkst bei der Prüfung von Implantaten, Instrumenten und Verpackungen im Bereich Medizintechnik mit.
Du analysierst Testergebnisse und dokumentierst deine Erkenntnisse strukturiert für technische Prüfberichte.
Du unterstützt bei norm- und sicherheitsrelevanten Prüfberichten und lernst wichtige Qualitätsanforderungen kennen.
Du arbeitest in Forschungs- und Entwicklungsprojekten mit erfahrenen Ingenieur:innen und Fachexpert:innen zusammen.
Das bringst du mit
Du befindest dich in einem Masterstudium der Medizintechnik, des Maschinenbaus, Biomedical Engineering, der Werkstoffwissenschaften oder eines vergleichbaren ingenieurwissenschaftlichen Studiengangs.
Du hast erste Kenntnisse in Anatomie , Werkstoffkunde oder Biomechanik .
Du interessierst dich für Produkttests , Medizintechnik , Forschung und Entwicklung.
Du arbeitest sorgfältig, strukturiert und möchtest Verantwortung in praxisnahen Projekten übernehmen.
Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse (C1) und gute Englischkenntnisse (B2).
Das erwartet dich
Vergütete sechsmonatige Abschlussarbeit
Start: März oder April 2027
Standort: Schönkirchen (bei Kiel)
Flexible Arbeitszeiten und attraktive Urlaubsregelung
Mentoring und Training zur Unterstützung deiner Entwicklung
Praxisnahe Projekte mit realem Impact in einem internationalen Umfeld
Bitte beachte: Deine Abschlussarbeit beschäftigt sich ggf. mit aktuellen und sensiblen Entwicklungsthemen, daher ist eine Vertraulichkeitsvereinbarung (Sperrvermerk) erforderlich. Deine konkreten Aufgaben können abhängig vom final ausgewählten Thema variieren.
Bewerbungsprozess
Bitte lade alle Bewerbungsunterlagen (notwendig ist ein kurzes Anschreiben, aktueller Lebenslauf und Notenübersicht) entweder als eine zusammengefasste Datei oder als separate Dateien im Bereich „Lebenslauf/CV“ des Bewerbungsformulars hoch. Ein nachträgliches Hochladen weiterer Dokumente ist leider nicht möglich.
Unser Auswahlprozess ist einfach und transparent:
1. Prüfung deiner Bewerbung
2. Kurzes telefonisches Kennenlerngespräch mit unserem University Talent Acquisition Team
3. Einstündiges Videointerview mit dem Hiring Team
Vielfalt ist uns wichtig. Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen von Menschen ungeachtet ihrer ethnischen, nationalen oder sozialen Herkunft, ihres Geschlechts, einer Behinderung, ihres Alters oder ihrer sexuellen Identität.
